title: Installing a Water-Saving Dual-Flush Toilet: leak-testing, removal, and replacement

locations.name: California
locations.basis: explicit mention in transcript: 'code here in California'

summary: This Old House walks through diagnosing a high-water-use, mid-century toilet and replacing it with a modern, water-saving dual-flush model. The segment demonstrates a blue-dye leak-test to confirm a tank-to-bowl leak, explains the water-use difference between a 1959-era toilet and contemporary units, and then shows the removal of the old fixture, preparation of the floor flange with wax ring and closet bolts, and the installation of a new tank-and-bowl assembly plus seat. The finished portion highlights the dual-flush mechanism with two levers offering 1.6 GPF for a full flush and 1.1 GPF for liquids, illustrating the practical water-savings achieved by upgrading.
topics: modern toilet water usage (1.6 GPF full flush)
cast iron flange and Johnny/closet bolts

sections.title: Leak testing and leak-diagnosis with dye
concepts: flapper tightness inferred from dye in bowl
assessing water waste from a leaking flush mechanism
sections.description: The presenter discusses a common symptom of a leaking toilet—water running at unexpected times—and demonstrates a simple dye test: add blue food coloring to the tank and wait about 20 minutes to see if color appears in the bowl, indicating leakage from the tank to the bowl due to an imperfect seal.

sections.title: Old toilet removal and new toilet installation (preparation and mounting)
concepts: cast iron flange and Johnny/closet bolts
warding off sewer gas through wax seal
sections.description: After ensuring all water is drained, the old toilet is detached by removing bolts and disconnecting the water line. The new toilet is prepared: tank-to-bowl assembly is joined with brass tank bolts and a gasket, the wax ring seals the bowl-to-flange connection, and the toilet seat is installed. The section also introduces the cast-iron flange and Johnny bolts as the mounting reference and explains the seal that prevents sewer gas and wastewater from escaping.

sections.title: Dual-flush mechanism and water-savings explanation
sections.description: The new toilet features two levers: the chrome lever for a full 1.6 gallons-per-flush and a secondary lever (green) for a liquids-only flush at about 1.1 GPF. The host highlights this as roughly a 70% reduction in water usage for liquids and a substantial saving compared to the old toilet, illustrating practical water efficiency gains.
